categories.label: Make a cluster
categories.line: Create, list and break local clusters with kind.
categories.intro: A cluster is a control plane that decides and nodes that run your containers. kind builds one on your laptop, each node a Docker container.

story.hook: Teammate: "Your app works on your laptop, now let's get it running on an actual multi-node cluster."
story.break: Running Docker containers directly on one machine gives you no failover or scheduling across nodes.
story.fix: Write a 3-node kind config (1 control-plane + 2 workers) and spin up the cluster with kind create cluster.
story.verify: Run kubectl get nodes -o wide until all three nodes report Ready.

categories.label: Deploy an app
categories.line: Run containers as Deployments, Jobs and one-off Pods.
categories.intro: A Deployment keeps a set of identical Pods running. Create one with a single command, or describe it in a YAML file and apply it.

story.hook: Teammate: "Uh oh, our bare Pod crashed and lost its state, and users still can't reach it from outside!"
story.break: A standalone Pod (kubectl run) is mortal: if it crashes or gets deleted, nothing brings it back.
story.fix: Create a Deployment so Kubernetes maintains 3 replicas automatically, then expose it with a Service.
story.verify: Delete one Pod and watch kubectl get pods -o wide spin up a replacement, then open localhost:8080.

categories.label: Scale and update
categories.intro: Change how many Pods run and which image they run. A Deployment replaces Pods a few at a time, so the app stays up.

story.hook: Teammate: "Traffic just spiked 10x, our single Pod is choking, and we also need to ship v1.27 without downtime!"
story.break: One replica can't handle the load, and restarting everything at once drops live user requests.
story.fix: Scale up replicas with kubectl scale, then roll out the new image gradually, or roll back if it breaks.
story.verify: Check kubectl rollout status deployment/web and confirm all replicas are Ready.

categories.label: Reach your app
categories.line: Services and port-forwarding from your laptop.
categories.intro: Pods come and go with new IPs. A Service gives them one stable name, and port-forward brings it to your laptop.

story.hook: Teammate: "The Pod restarted and its IP changed again, our frontend can't hardcode Pod IPs!"
story.break: Every time a Deployment replaces a Pod, Kubernetes assigns it a brand-new internal IP address.
story.fix: Create a ClusterIP Service that tracks healthy Pods by label, and use port-forward to test from your laptop.
story.verify: Run kubectl get endpointslices to see the Service automatically pointing at your live Pod IPs.

categories.label: Config and secrets
categories.intro: Keep settings out of the image. ConfigMaps hold plain values, Secrets hold passwords and tokens.

story.hook: Teammate: "Wait, our database password and environment flags are hardcoded right inside the container image!"
story.break: Rebuilding a Docker image just to change a config flag or rotate a password is slow and unsafe.
story.fix: Move non-sensitive settings into a ConfigMap and credentials into a Secret, injected at runtime.
story.verify: Inspect the running Pod environment or volume mounts to confirm settings loaded cleanly.

categories.label: Debug a pod
categories.intro: When a Pod misbehaves, describe it, read its logs and its events. Those three answer most questions.

story.hook: Pager alert at 2 AM: "Production Pods are stuck Pending or CrashLoopBackOff, checkout is returning 503!"
story.break: kubectl get pods only tells you something is wrong, not why it happened.
story.fix: Run kubectl describe pod for scheduling/probe events, kubectl logs for app crashes, and exec inside if needed.
story.verify: Pinpoint the exact FailedScheduling or container error message and fix the manifest.

categories.label: Namespaces and labels
categories.intro: Namespaces split one cluster into rooms. Labels tag objects so commands and controllers can pick them out.

story.hook: Teammate: "Staging and production Pods are mixed together in default, we need clean isolation and automation."
story.break: Putting every team and environment in the default namespace makes cleanup and policies risky.
story.fix: Separate workloads into dedicated Namespaces and tag them with labels so controllers know what to manage.
story.verify: Query resources by namespace and label selector (-l) to verify clean isolation.

categories.label: Helm charts
categories.line: Install packaged apps in one line.
categories.intro: Helm installs packaged apps, called charts, with one command, and removes them just as easily.

categories.label: Shell setup
categories.line: Versions, contexts, aliases and tab completion.
categories.intro: Before the first cluster, check the tools answer and set up your shell. An alias and tab completion save thousands of keystrokes.

categories.label: Look inside
categories.line: etcd, the runtime, kubelet logs and the API.
categories.intro: Follow a request below kubectl: the API server, etcd, the container runtime and the kubelet.

categories.label: Controllers in Go
categories.intro: A controller watches the cluster and fixes what drifts. These commands set up a client-go project.

categories.label: Clean up
categories.intro: Delete what you made so the next exercise starts clean.

commands.desc: Creates a cluster from a config file. With the 3-node file you get 1 control-plane and 2 workers.

recipes.title: Make a multi-node cluster
recipes.intro: kind reads a small YAML file that lists node roles. Add or remove `- role: worker` lines to change the node count.

steps.code:
cat > kind-3node.yaml <<'EOF'
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
name: klu
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
- role: worker
EOF
steps.ps:
@'
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
name: klu
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
- role: worker
'@ | Set-Content kind-3node.yaml

steps.text: Wait until all three nodes are Ready

recipes.title: Deploy from a YAML file
recipes.intro: The declarative way: describe the Deployment and Service in one file, apply it, change it, apply again.

steps.code:
cat > web.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
  - port: 80
EOF
steps.ps:
@'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
  - port: 80
'@ | Set-Content web.yaml
